summary: The final R step reaches the unported do_wear.c Amulet_off() branch. C removes the worn amulet through setworn(NULL, W_AMUL) before off_msg() formats “You were wearing a hexagonal amulet.”; JavaScript records the call as unported and skips both the reflection property/slot removal and message. This is a whole-function file port. Reflection removal does not identify the amulet: that switch arm leaves mkn false, so makeknown() is not called.

source.branch: When a worn amulet of reflection is removed through the R command, armor_or_accessory_off() calls Amulet_off(). Its AMULET_OF_REFLECTION switch arm has no effect-specific body; the shared tail clears W_AMUL through setworn() before calling off_msg(). With verbose output enabled, doname() therefore formats the item without a “being worn” suffix. This branch does not set mkn or identify the amulet.
callers: do_wear.c armor_or_accessory_off() calls Amulet_off() when the selected item is uamul; doremring() (R) and dotakeoff() (T) reach this helper.
do_wear.c do_takeoff() calls Amulet_off() for the WORN_AMUL arm of the multi-item takeoff command.
steal.c remove_worn_item() calls Amulet_off() when a worn amulet is removed during theft.
pray.c offer_real_amulet() calls Amulet_off() before consuming the worn Amulet of Yendor.
dependencies: worn.c setworn(NULL, W_AMUL) is the property and slot transition: it clears uamul and the object W_AMUL bit, removes the object-provided extrinsic property (reflection for this case), and calls update_inventory() and recalc_telepat_range().

do_wear.c off_msg(amul) calls doname(amul) and prints only when flags.verbose is true. Amulet_off() calls it after setworn(), so the reported item name has no worn suffix; this is separate from setworn() refreshing inventory.

do_wear.c makeknown(amul->otyp) is conditional on mkn. AMULET_OF_REFLECTION does not set mkn, so removing this amulet does not reveal its type. Other Amulet_off() switch arms set mkn when their observable effects warrant discovery.
do_wear.c see_monsters() handles removal of ESP amulets after clearing the slot and sending the early off message.

region_danger(), cant_drown(), drown(), and hliquid() support the magical-breathing branch. region_danger() and cant_drown() results control branches; drown() is explicitly called with its result discarded.
do_wear.c find_ac() handles removal of an amulet of guarding.
float_vs_flight(), is_pool_or_lava(), Is_waterlevel(), Is_airlevel(), and spoteffects(TRUE) support the flying-amulet branch and its landing effects.

evidence: At the examined root commit 6d2c675aad59f170ec44980d6afce47f08ae7423, `.cache/synthetic-scans/v15/wizard-removes-reflection-amulet-p-slot.json` records the only mismatch at segment 0, step 43, key R: C has Y at row 0, column 0 and JavaScript has a space. Its saved evaluation `challenges/evaluations/20261001022926-v15.json` reports 43/44 screens matched, all 2307 RNG calls matched, all 44 cursors matched, and one remaining screen.

The C recording `challenges/cases/v15/wizard-removes-reflection-amulet-p-slot.session.json`, segment 0, steps 40-43, shows the wish completing, P selecting the amulet, p confirming “a hexagonal amulet (being worn),” and R producing “You were wearing a hexagonal amulet.” in the C screen. The saved diagnostic shows the corresponding JavaScript final row begins blank.

The frozen source at the assigned root commit, `nethack-c/upstream/src/do_wear.c:1768-1829`, defines the whole `armor_or_accessory_off()` owner. Its amulet arm calls `Amulet_off()` at :1819 and returns ECMD_TIME; `dotakeoff()` and `doremring()` both route selected items through this helper. The command recording reaches it through doremring().

The actionable whole-function scope is `nethack-c/upstream/src/do_wear.c:1090-1190`, `Amulet_off()`. The AMULET_OF_REFLECTION case at :1105-1110 has no body; the shared tail at :1183-1189 clears W_AMUL with setworn(), then calls off_msg(amul). At the examined JavaScript source, `js/do_wear.js:3626-3630` instead records `note_unported('do_wear.c Amulet_off')`, so it skips both state removal and feedback.

`nethack-c/upstream/src/worn.c:73-145`, `setworn()`, supplies the property and inventory semantics: replacing the W_AMUL slot clears the object’s worn mask and its oc_oprop extrinsic bit, installs the null slot, then refreshes inventory and telepathy range. The reflection property disappears as part of this operation; Amulet_off() does not separately alter or identify it.

Identification and display are distinct from that state transition. In do_wear.c, `mkn` starts false and the reflection arm never sets it, so the final guarded makeknown() at :1187 does not run. `off_msg()` at :68-73 runs after setworn(); it formats the now-unworn object with doname(), yielding the C message without a “being worn” suffix.

Direct C callers found in the frozen source are `do_wear.c armor_or_accessory_off()` (:1819), `do_wear.c do_takeoff()` (:2878), `steal.c remove_worn_item()` (:265), and `pray.c offer_real_amulet()` (:1536). The associated JavaScript branches include the missing call in `js/do_wear.js:3626-3630` and a second unported gap in `js/steal.js:339-340`; the source port must preserve existing caller order where these paths are wired.
